input_text: has anyone else found that cbd does basically nothing for joint pain? i have ra and was hoping it might help me get through the nights without taking extra ibuprofen, but after a few weeks of trying different doses i honestly feel like i'm just spending money on flavored oil. the weird part is that even the supposedly "pure" cbd made me feel foggy and a little more nauseous, which is the last thing i need on methotrexate days. maybe i'm just not a good candidate for it, but at this point cbd seems more annoying than helpful. anyone else have zero luck with it?

i tried a low-dose thc edible last weekend because several people said it would help with sleep and stiffness from ankylosing spondylitis. nope. it made my heart race, my anxiety shoot up, and i spent half the night convinced every tiny sensation in my body meant i was having some kind of reaction. the pain was still there in the morning, just with added paranoia and a gross hungover feeling. i know thc works great for some people, but for me it seems to make everything worse instead of better.

just wanted to vent a little: marijuana has been a bad experience every single time i've tried it since getting my lupus diagnosis. i keep hearing that it can help with appetite and pain, but all i get is a weird head rush, dry mouth, and this super uncomfortable sense that my joints hurt more because i'm paying attention to them too much. one time i even felt like my hands were swelling up more, though maybe it was just anxiety. either way, marijuana is not the miracle some people make it out to be for me.

i'm honestly jealous of people who say weed helps their flare symptoms, because for me it just makes me feel off. i have psoriatic arthritis and tried vaping a tiny amount to see if it would take the edge off my knee and ankle pain. instead i got dizzy, kind of shaky, and weirdly aware of every ache in my body. i also slept terribly. after that i stopped trying because weed just feels like it adds another problem on top of the pain rather than helping with it.

my rheumatologist didn't push it, but a friend kept telling me to look into medical marijuana for my constant inflammation and sleep issues. i gave it a real shot and honestly regretted it. the product labels made everything sound very controlled and "medical," but all i noticed was brain fog, a racing mind, and no meaningful change in my stiffness. i was expecting at least some relief with the medical marijuana route, but it felt like an expensive experiment that made me less functional the next day. disappointing.

anyone else get weird flares from cbd? i started a small dose tincture for joint pain because my rheum suggested i "try something gentle" before upping meds. instead of calming things down, the cbd seems to make my heart pound, my face feel hot, and my mouth even drier than usual. i have sjogren's and ra and i honestly expected at least *some* help with sleep or pain, but after 3 nights i feel more wired and sore. i keep seeing people say cbd is super safe, so i'm wondering if i'm just one of the unlucky ones. has anyone had actual worsening symptoms from cbd or am i missing something? cubby? maybe it was the carrier oil? no clue.

my lupus symptoms have been awful lately, especially the fatigue and hand pain, and i used to think marijuana helped me relax a little. now it just makes me feel foggy, anxious, and somehow more aware of every ache in my body. the last two times i tried a tiny hit i ended up nauseous and staring at the ceiling convinced my joints were swelling up even more. i know people online swear by marijuana for autoimmune pain, but i don't get that at all. is this something that happens once you already have inflammation issues, or is it just not for me anymore?

i stopped smoking weed for a month because i was hoping it was contributing to my dry eyes and constant fatigue. honestly, i think i feel better off it. every time i start again, my mouth turns into sandpaper, my chest feels tight, and my pain doesn't improve enough to justify it. i have suspected sjogren's and some raynaud's stuff going on, so maybe weed just isn't a good match for me. i feel kind of silly because a lot of people in my life act like it should be the magical answer for chronic pain, but for me it's just been irritating and disappointing. anyone else end up quitting for the same reason?

i tried a low-dose thc gummy on a night when my ankylosing spondylitis pain was making sleep impossible. bad idea. it didn't help me relax, it made my whole body feel buzzy and my knees hurt more, like my brain was magnifying every little symptom. i also got super dizzy standing up, which is already a problem for me because of possible dysautonomia. the weirdest part is that the thc didn't even touch the pain, but it did leave me feeling nauseated and anxious for hours. has anyone with autoimmune issues had thc make you feel worse instead of better? i'm starting to think it just isn't worth the gamble.

my doctor brought up medical marijuana for neuropathy and appetite, but i've had such a bad reaction to anything cannabis-related that i'm hesitant. i tried a vape from a friend once and it honestly made my tremor worse, my thoughts scattered, and my joints feel more inflamed somehow. with my ra and celiac issues i already have enough random symptoms to track without adding another thing that leaves me feeling out of it. i know medical marijuana helps a lot of people, and i wish i were one of them, but right now it mostly seems to make my body feel louder and less manageable. did anyone else get nothing but side effects from it?

anyone else get absolutely nothing out of cbd? i have sjogren's and was hoping it would take the edge off the night pain and help me sleep, but the capsules just gave me a weird stomach ache and zero relief. i also hate how often people act like cbd is some magic fix for autoimmune stuff. my rheum already has me on meds that are actually doing something, so i'd rather not keep wasting money on another bottle of disappointment.

i tried cannabis for the first time in a long while because my psoriatic arthritis has been flaring hard and i was desperate for something to help. instead of calming anything down it made me super anxious, my hands felt shaky, and the pain was still there when i woke up. honestly it was just an expensive way to feel worse for a few hours. not for me.

i know people swear by weed for inflammatory pain, but in my case it seems to do the opposite. i have ankylosing spondylitis and when i smoke at night i wake up feeling groggier, more stiff, and weirdly more aware of every ache in my back. it also makes my throat dry enough that i cough all night, which is the last thing i need when my chest wall is already sore. disappointing, because i really wanted it to work.

my rheumatologist's office keeps hinting that medical marijuana might be worth trying for my ra, but i do not understand why it keeps getting suggested when my experience has been so bad. i tried a tincture from a dispensary and all it did was make my heart race and give me a foggy headache. no pain reduction, no better sleep, just feeling out of it and annoyed. i wish people would stop treating it like a universal solution.

has anyone else had thc make their symptoms feel worse instead of better? i took a very small edible for lupus pain and ended up nauseated, dizzy, and extra sensitive to every little joint twinge. it didn't touch the inflammation at all. after that i was basically done with it. maybe it helps some people, but for me thc was just uncomfortable and not worth repeating.

has anyone else felt like cbd just does absolutely nothing? i'm 29, seronegative ra, and i keep getting told to “try cbd first” by people who have never had a flare in their life. i bought tinctures, gummies, and a topical roll-on, gave it a real shot for about 6 weeks, and all i got was a lighter wallet and weird stomach upset. no change in morning stiffness, no change in swelling, not even a little help sleeping. honestly i'm annoyed that it gets recommended like it’s some magic fix when it isn’t touching my inflammation at all.

i thought THC would be a better option for pain and sleep while i'm waiting on a rheum appointment for possible lupus, but it has been a disaster for me. even tiny doses make my heart race, my mouth go super dry, and my anxiety goes through the roof. the pain is still there, plus now i'm just more aware of it because i'm panicking. i really wanted this to be helpful and instead it just makes me feel worse and kind of trapped in my own body. not worth it for me.

my doctor suggested medical marijuana for my psoriatic arthritis when celebrex stopped helping, so i tried it with an open mind. i was hoping for at least some relief with the constant hand pain and back stiffness. instead it made me groggy, foggy, and weirdly more sensitive to every ache. i also had a terrible next-day headache and felt completely useless at work. i know some people swear by it, but for me medical marijuana was just another thing that didn't help and made me miserable.

i'm honestly so tired of people acting like weed is the answer to everything. i have sjogren's and severe dry eyes/dry mouth already, so when i tried smoking a few times i ended up feeling like sandpaper from the inside out. my throat hurt, my eyes burned more, and the pain relief was basically zero. it just seems like one more thing that adds symptoms instead of easing them. maybe it's fine for other people, but for autoimmune dryness? absolutely not for me.

does anyone else feel like cannabis makes their autoimmune symptoms spiral instead of helping? i have ra and mild pots, and every time i try an edible for sleep i end up with a pounding heartbeat, dizziness, and the next day my joints feel even more inflamed. i kept trying different brands because people kept saying i just needed to find the right one, but at this point i'm done. cannabis has been the opposite of helpful and i'm frustrated i wasted so much money on it.

anyone else feel like cbd is basically a scam for inflammatory arthritis? i’ve been taking gummies for a few weeks because everybody in my family swore it would “take the edge off,” but all it’s done is lighten my wallet. zero change in the morning stiffness, zero change in the swelling, maybe even made me groggy. i’m not expecting a miracle, just something that actually does something. if it helps you, great, but for me cbd has been a total dud.

quick question for people with sjogren’s: does thc always make the dryness worse or am i just extra unlucky? i tried a tiny amount last night hoping it might help me relax and sleep through the joint pain, but my mouth and eyes got so miserable i was up drinking water every ten minutes. it didn’t even help the pain much, just made me anxious and sticky-dry. honestly i regret bothering with it.

i know people mean well when they recommend weed for everything, but i wish they’d stop telling me it’s the answer for lupus pain. i gave it a fair try a few times and all it did was make me feel spacey, heart racing, and weirdly more aware of the ache in my hands. not a fun combo. maybe it works for some folks, but weed and my body clearly do not get along.

has anyone else been pushed toward medical marijuana by every friend and their cousin after an autoimmune diagnosis? i’m honestly frustrated. i tried a tincture because i was desperate during a bad flare and it made me feel foggy, nauseated, and kind of panicky without touching the inflammation. i’m tired of being told to “just try cannabis” like it’s somehow replacing actual treatment. i’d rather stick with meds that have evidence.

marijuana is getting recommended to me nonstop since my ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis, and i’m over it. maybe i’m sensitive, but the couple times i tried it i got a headache and my pain actually felt more intense once the novelty wore off. i also hate how people act like saying it didn’t help means i’m not trying hard enough. it did not help. at all.

has anyone else had cbd just do absolutely nothing? i picked up a tincture and a topical from a dispensary after my rheum nurse suggested i “try the gentle route” for hand and wrist pain. after 3 weeks the only thing i noticed was an empty wallet and a weird stomach ache. my joints still feel like they’re on fire, and the cbd didn’t touch the morning stiffness or the nerve-y pain in my fingers. honestly i’m annoyed because everyone online talks like it’s some miracle. maybe it helps other people, but for me it was a total waste.

i tried a low-dose thc gummy last night because i was desperate for sleep during this flare, and it backfired hard. instead of relaxing, i got super wired, my heart was racing, and my pain felt louder somehow. i ended up staring at the ceiling for hours with my wrists throbbing and my mouth so dry i had to keep drinking water. maybe thc works for some folks, but it made an already miserable night way worse. i’m done experimenting with it for now.

my new rheumatologist mentioned medical marijuana as one option while we wait to see if the biologic kicks in, but i’m pretty skeptical at this point. i’ve tried two different products from a licensed clinic and both left me foggy, nauseous, and somehow still in pain. the extra brain fog is the worst part because i already struggle with fatigue from psoriatic arthritis. i know people mean well when they recommend it, but medical marijuana has not been a good fit for me at all.

weed used to be something i could tolerate socially, but since my sjogren's symptoms ramped up it just seems to make everything worse. the dry mouth gets unbearable, my eyes feel grittier, and my throat is irritated for hours afterward. i also notice more joint aching the next day, which is the last thing i need when i’m already dealing with inflammation and exhaustion. i’ve basically stopped completely because it adds problems instead of helping.

i hate that i even have to ask this, but has anyone had cannabis make their autoimmune symptoms feel more intense? i tried an edible hoping it would take the edge off the pain from my hands and knees, but i got anxious, my muscles felt tight, and i ended up hyperfocused on every ache in my body. it didn’t help sleep either. i’m starting to think cannabis just isn’t for me, which is frustrating because i really wanted something that would calm things down without all the side effects.

has anyone else found that cbd just does absolutely nothing for joint pain? i have psoriatic arthritis and got talked into trying tinctures, gummies, and a topical from a local shop because everyone swears by it. i gave it a fair shot for a few weeks and honestly all i got was a lighter wallet and a weird stomach ache. no change in stiffness, no change in the morning pain, nothing. if anything i was more annoyed because i kept hoping i was finally finding something that would let me cut back on naproxen. maybe i bought the wrong brand or maybe cbd just isn't my thing, but i don't get the hype at all.

i know people love talking about cannabis like it's some miracle for autoimmune pain, but it made my symptoms feel worse. i have lupus and after trying an edible one night i woke up feeling super foggy, nauseous, and somehow more achy than usual. the next day my hands were puffy and i was just miserable. i wasn't even trying to get high, just wanted something to help me sleep through a flare. instead i spent half the night panicking because my heart was racing and my joints felt on fire. maybe it helps other people, but for me cannabis was a bad tradeoff and i'm not touching it again.

thc is apparently not my friend. i tried a low-dose tincture for back pain and it turned into one of the worst evenings i've had in months. my pain didn't calm down at all, i got dizzy, and then the anxiety kicked in hard enough that i was convinced i was having some kind of reaction. my shoulders and hips were already inflamed from a flare, and the thc just made me feel hyper-aware of every single sensation in my body. i kept waiting for the relaxing part people talk about, but it never came. ended up in bed with a heating pad and zero relief.

i stopped smoking weed a while back because it was making everything harder, not easier. i have ra and the biggest problem for me was that it would leave me exhausted and glued to the couch, which sounds fine until you realize i was skipping meals, sleeping weird hours, and then waking up with even more stiffness. the pain in my knees and wrists didn't improve, and my brain felt so slow that i couldn't keep up with work or even basic errands. i kept telling myself it was helping me unwind, but really it just made me feel gross and less motivated to take care of myself. not worth it.

i asked my rheumatologist about medical marijuana because i was desperate to get through the night without waking up every hour. unfortunately it was a total disappointment. the first couple of tries left me groggy, spacey, and weirdly more sensitive to pain, like my whole body was buzzing in a bad way. i also felt really dry-mouthed and anxious, which made sleeping even harder. i know some people in this sub say it helps their lupus or sjogren's symptoms, but my experience with medical marijuana has been the opposite. i would rather stick with my regular meds than feel drugged and still hurt.

anyone else feel like cbd is basically useless for inflammatory arthritis pain? i bought two different tinctures and a salve because i was desperate after a flare in my wrists and knees, and all it did was make my wallet lighter. the lotion smelled nice but the actual pain was exactly the same an hour later. i know people swear by it, but for me it just feels like expensive tea oil. if anything, the one with cbd made my stomach kind of gross, which is the last thing i need when i'm already taking naproxen and prednisone. just wondering if i'm the odd one out or if some of us really do get zero benefit from cbd.

quick question for people with sjögren's: does thc make your dry mouth absolutely unbearable? i tried a low-dose edible because i was having a rough night with joint pain and couldn't sleep, but my mouth turned into the sahara and swallowing felt weird for hours. it didn't even help much with the pain, honestly. i ended up sipping water nonstop and still felt like sandpaper. i keep seeing thc recommended in lupus/ra groups and i'm confused because it seems to make one of my worst symptoms much worse. maybe i'm just sensitive, but i don't think thc is going to be part of my toolkit.

i know weed helps a lot of people here, but i think my body hates it. every time i've tried it for pain or nausea, i get weirdly anxious and then my heart starts racing, which sends my fatigue and muscle aches into overdrive. the last time was after a long day of labs and a rheum appointment; instead of relaxing, i spent the whole evening convinced every twinge meant something terrible. not fun, not helpful, and definitely not worth it for me. does anyone else feel like weed just makes them notice every symptom 10x more?

my rheumatologist suggested i look into medical marijuana for night pain, so i tried to keep an open mind. honestly, i think it's been a bust. the gummies made me dizzy, foggy, and weirdly more aware of my hip pain instead of less aware of it. i also woke up feeling super groggy, like i had slept in a swamp. i was hoping it would be a gentler option than stronger meds, but so far it has just given me side effects and no real relief. maybe i'm missing the right dose or type, but right now medical marijuana feels like another thing my body doesn't cooperate with.

i'm curious if anyone with ra/sjogren's has had bad luck with cannabis and inflammation? i tried a couple different strains because people in my support group kept saying it would help with sleep and pain, but all i got was a headache, a dry throat, and this awful wired feeling that made my joints seem even more tender. i was hoping cannabis would take the edge off the flare i'm in, but instead it just made me feel off and more irritable. at this point i'd rather stick with heat packs and boring old otc meds than keep experimenting with something that doesn't seem to agree with me.

has anyone else had weird reactions to cbd with ra? i tried a tincture last week because my wrists and knees have been flaring nonstop, and instead of calming anything down it made me feel kind of shaky, nauseous, and more achy the next day. i kept waiting for the supposed anti-inflammatory effect and honestly got nothing but a headache and worse fatigue. i know some people swear by cbd but it feels like it does the opposite for me. is that just me being sensitive, or can cbd actually make pain feel worse?

i’m honestly disappointed with medical marijuana so far. i have scleroderma and terrible hand pain, plus the usual insomnia from being uncomfortable all night, so i got my card thinking it might help me cut back on otc meds. instead it just left me foggy, anxious, and somehow even more aware of every little joint pain. i tried different strains, different doses, gummies, vape, all of it. nothing seemed worth it. if anything, i spent money to feel worse and then had to nap off the side effects. does anyone actually tolerate it with autoimmune disease?

thc and i do not get along at all. i have sjogren’s and was hoping it would help with pain and sleep, but every time i try it i get this gross racing-heart feeling, dry mouth that is somehow even worse than usual, and a kind of panicky body buzz that makes my joints feel more sensitive. it’s like my nervous system is already on fire and thc pours gasoline on it. i know plenty of people use it for pain, but for me it’s been a complete fail. anyone else get more inflammation-feeling after thc?

weird question maybe, but does weed make anyone else feel physically worse instead of relaxed? i have lupus and usually my flares come with fatigue, body aches, and that all-over flu feeling. i tried smoking a tiny amount because several people told me it might help with appetite and pain. nope. my head got heavy, my chest felt uncomfortable, and my skin/joints felt extra tender for hours. i was not even high in a pleasant way, just miserable and more aware of how bad i felt. i’m done pretending weed is a miracle for me.

i wish cannabis helped my inflammatory arthritis like people say it does, but it really doesn’t. i’ve experimented with edibles and a couple different vape products, and the result is always the same: more brain fog, more dizziness, and a strange uptick in pain sensitivity later that night or the next morning. i’m not anti-anything, i just wanted a break from the constant aches. instead cannabis has been another thing i have to recover from. has anyone else found it actually aggravates their symptoms rather than helping?

anyone else have absolutely no luck with cbd? i’ve got sjögren’s and inflammatory arthritis, and every time i try a gummy or tincture i end up feeling weirdly jittery, more nauseous, and somehow even drier than before. people keep telling me it’s "gentle" and that i just need to find the right dose, but at this point i’m annoyed because it feels like it does the opposite of what it’s supposed to do. i’m not looking for miracle cures, just something that won’t make me feel worse. cbd has been a disappointment for me.

my rheumatologist didn’t mind that i asked about trying marijuana for pain, but honestly i wish i hadn’t bothered. i have ra and the first couple times i used it, my joints didn’t really improve at all; instead i got foggy, anxious, and then slept terribly. the next day my stiffness was worse because i was exhausted. i know a lot of people swear by it, but for me marijuana just turned into another thing that made managing symptoms harder. has anyone else had it backfire like that?

quick vent: thc is not my friend. i have lupus and was hoping it might take the edge off the pain so i could cut back on nsaids, but even tiny amounts make my heart race and my head feel floaty in a bad way. i also get more aware of every ache instead of less, which is the opposite of what i wanted. it’s frustrating because everyone in my circle talks about thc like it’s some perfect solution, but all i’ve gotten is side effects and regret.

has anyone had a bad experience with medical marijuana and dry eyes/mouth? i’m being worked up for sjogren’s and i thought it might help with sleep and pain, but it made me wake up feeling like i had sand in my eyes and cotton in my mouth. i also felt groggy all morning, which is a disaster when i already struggle with fatigue from inflammation. i gave it a fair try, but medical marijuana seems to make the symptoms i’m already battling even more annoying. maybe i’m just not a good candidate for it.

i’m tired of people telling me cannabis is "natural" so it must be harmless. for me, with psa and pretty bad anxiety on top of it, it just made everything messier: worse dry mouth, worse sleep, and a couple of scary episodes where i felt panicky and couldn’t settle down. the pain relief was minimal at best. i’m not judging anyone who uses it, but cannabis has been a letdown in my case and i’m done pretending it’s helping.

Has anyone else had a weird reaction to cbd? I tried a tincture and a cream because my rheum friend kept saying it might take the edge off my morning stiffness, but all it did was make me feel lightheaded and kind of gross. My joints still hurt, my sleep was unchanged, and the constant aftertaste made me nauseous enough to skip dinner. Honestly I’m annoyed I spent money on it when a heating pad helped more.

I know some people swear by marijuana for autoimmune pain, but for me it has been the opposite. I have sjogren's and pretty bad fatigue, and every time I try it I get more dry-mouthed, more anxious, and the brain fog turns into full-on uselessness. I end up staring at the wall feeling stoned and uncomfortable while my wrists still ache. Not worth it at all, at least for me.

Does thc always make inflammation feel worse for anyone else? I have psoriatic arthritis and tried a low-dose edible on a night my knee was flaring. Instead of helping, it made my heart race and I felt super aware of every twinge in my body. I didn’t even sleep well because I kept fixating on whether I was having some bad reaction. Pretty disappointed, honestly.

I’m so frustrated because weed just does not agree with me. I’ve got lupus and was hoping it would help on the nights when the joint pain and headaches are bad, but all I get is feeling dizzy, paranoid, and weirdly more sensitive to every ache. It also makes me cough like crazy and then my chest hurts for the rest of the evening. I’m done trying to force it to work.

My rheumatologist said I could ask a dispensary about medical marijuana for breakthrough pain, so I gave it a shot after months of trying to get through a flare. Big mistake. It didn’t touch the pain, made me nauseated, and I woke up the next day feeling even more sluggish than usual. I’m not against it for other people, but for my ra it was just another thing that failed and left me irritated.

anyone else feel like cbd is basically a fancy placebo? i keep getting told to try it for my ankylosing spondylitis pain and morning stiffness, so i gave it a real shot: tincture under the tongue, gummies at night, even the cream on my hands. all it did was make my wallet lighter and give me a weird bitter taste. no change in the burning in my SI joints, no help with sleep, nothing. i’m not anti-anything if it helps, but at this point cbd feels like another thing people suggest instead of actually dealing with the inflammation. has anyone with actual inflammatory arthritis found it useful, or am i wasting my time here?

i’m so tired of the “have you tried cannabis?” advice from everyone who suddenly becomes an expert the second they hear lupus. i did try it, and for me it made the brain fog and anxiety way worse, which is honestly the last thing i need during a flare. my heart felt like it was racing and i could not relax at all. the pain was still there, plus i was staring at the ceiling feeling paranoid and useless. maybe it works for some people, but cannabis is not my miracle option and i’m annoyed that it gets pushed like it’s the answer to everything.

f23 with ra here. i used to smoke marijuana on and off in college, and every time i’ve gone back to it recently it seems to make me feel gross the next day. the joint pain is still there, but now i’m also nauseous, dehydrated, and even more tired than usual. i tried a tiny amount thinking maybe i just overdid it before, but nope, same thing. not worth it for me. i’d rather take my naproxen and deal with the stiffness than spend half the night anxious and then wake up feeling like i got hit by a truck.

just venting: thc and i are apparently not friends. i have psoriatic arthritis and when i’m flaring, people keep telling me to try higher thc edibles for the pain. i’ve done that three times now and each time i ended up more sensitive, more restless, and honestly a little nauseated. instead of helping my hips and knees calm down, thc made me focus on every ache in my body until i was miserable. i know it helps some folks, but for me it seems to crank everything up. i’m over the suggestions at this point.

i know this will probably be unpopular, but medical marijuana has not been the helpful thing i hoped for after my sjogren’s diagnosis. i bought into the whole “natural relief” idea because i’m desperate for anything that helps with the dryness, fatigue, and hand pain. all it did was make me sleepy in a foggy, unpleasant way, and the dry mouth was honestly worse. my eyes still burned, my joints still hurt, and i felt too spaced out to function. i’m not saying nobody benefits, but medical marijuana has been a bust for me and i wish people would stop acting like it’s some guaranteed fix.

has anyone else had basically zero luck with cbd? i have psoriatic arthritis and tried a couple tinctures plus a topical cbd roll-on for about six weeks. not only did it not touch the pain in my hands/knees, but the oil made my stomach feel off and the cream gave me a weird rash behind my knee. i keep seeing people say it 'takes the edge off,' but for me cbd just feels expensive and useless. am i missing something, or is it just not worth the hype for inflammatory pain?

i'm starting to think thc is not my friend at all. i have sjogren's and some pretty nasty nerve pain, and a friend gave me a low-dose gummy because everyone swore it would help me relax and sleep. instead i got a pounding heart, worse dry mouth, and this awful spiral of anxiety where every joint ache felt 10x bigger. slept badly, woke up groggy, and the pain was still there. does thc do this to anyone else or am i just unusually sensitive?

super frustrated right now because weed keeps making my RA symptoms feel worse, not better. i used to smoke a little at night thinking it would help me unwind after work, but lately it just leaves me dehydrated, foggy, and weirdly more aware of every little ache in my wrists and shoulders. the worst part is the next morning i feel wiped out before i even get out of bed. i know some people with chronic pain swear by it, but i'm honestly done pretending weed is helping me.

my rheumatologist was fine with me trying medical marijuana for sleep and pain, so i figured why not. honestly it has been a disappointment. the first couple nights i felt mildly relaxed, then it started giving me a racing mind, dry eyes, and this heavy drained feeling the next day that made work impossible. my inflammatory back pain was still there too. i keep hearing about people getting real relief from medical marijuana, but in my case it seems to make me feel worse overall. anyone else have the opposite of the 'miracle cure' experience?

just wanted to vent a little: cannabis has been a total miss for my autoimmune stuff. i have lupus-like symptoms and pretty constant fatigue, and every time i try a small amount, i end up nauseous, sleepy in the wrong way, and more anxious about my symptoms instead of less. i even tried a balanced product because people said the ratio matters, but nope — still felt awful and useless. i’m not anti-anything, i just wish cannabis actually helped the way people on the internet claim it does.

anyone else feel like cbd is basically a very expensive placebo for inflammatory arthritis? i bought two different tinctures and a salve after reading so many reviews, gave it a solid month, and the only thing it improved was my wallet staying lighter. no change in morning stiffness, no real pain relief, and one of the drops even upset my stomach. i'm still on my normal meds, but i was hoping cbd might take the edge off on bad flare days. instead i just got tired of listening to friends tell me to "try natural stuff" like i hadn't already. does it actually work for anyone with ra, or am i just wasting money? cbd and joint pain

i tried thc gummies for sleep because prednisone has me feeling wired at night, and honestly it was a disaster. my heart started pounding, i felt weird and anxious, and the pain in my hands somehow felt louder. slept worse than usual, which is impressive because i thought nothing could beat 3am ra pain. maybe i'm just sensitive, but thc definitely did not calm anything down for me. it just made me feel out of it and more aware of every ache. has anyone else had thc make flares feel worse instead of better? not for me at all.

i know people swear by weed for autoimmune pain, but for me it has been the opposite. i have sjogren's and already deal with dry mouth all day, so smoking just turns my throat into sandpaper and makes talking miserable. i tried a small edible once too and got a racing mind, nausea, and zero relief in my joints. at this point i don't understand the hype. if anything, weed adds another problem i don't need. maybe i'm missing the right strain or method, but so far it has been a bad tradeoff.

my rheumatologist suggested i "look into medical marijuana" after i said i was still waking up in pain despite methotrexate and celecoxib. i did some research, paid for the card, went to a dispensary, and left feeling pretty disappointed. the oil they recommended did nothing for swelling and the vape made me cough so hard i hurt my ribs. i wanted to be open-minded, but medical marijuana has not helped my psoriatic arthritis one bit. if anything, it just gave me another thing to spend money on while my actual meds get adjusted.

does anyone else get annoyed when people act like cannabis is the answer to every chronic illness? i have lupus, neuropathy, and constant fatigue, and i tried a few different products because everyone around me kept saying it would be "game changing." nope. i mostly got a headache, brain fog, and this awful floaty feeling that made it harder to function at work. the pain was still there, just now with bonus dizziness. maybe cannabis helps some people, but it has not been a useful tool for me and i'm tired of being told i'm not trying hard enough.

honestly i'm so tired of everyone acting like cbd is some miracle answer for autoimmune pain. i've spent the last year trying gummies, tinctures, and a couple of overpriced creams for my hands and shoulders, and all i got was a lighter wallet and the same stiffness. the topical stuff smelled nice, sure, but it didn't touch the inflammation. if anything, the gummy made me groggy and weirdly nauseous the next morning. has anyone actually gotten real relief from cbd, or is this just another thing people tell us to buy because they don't know what lupus/ra pain feels like?

does weed make anyone else feel absolutely awful? i used to think it helped me sleep, but since my sjogren's got worse it just makes my mouth feel like i've swallowed sandpaper and my heart starts pounding. i tried a tiny amount last night for pain and ended up more anxious, more dry, and somehow even more aware of every joint ache in my body. not fun at all. i'm done pretending it's useful for me.

my rheumatologist suggested i "experiment" with cannabis for flare pain, so i gave it a fair shot. bad idea. i took what was supposed to be a low dose and spent the next few hours dizzy, shaky, and completely useless, with my brain fog turned up to 100. the pain never really changed, but my stomach did, and not in a good way. maybe it works for some people, but cannabis seems to do the opposite for me. i feel like i function worse every time i try it.

i know a lot of people in this sub swear by medical marijuana, but i just don't get it. it hasn't helped my inflammatory arthritis at all, and the side effects are miserable for me. i get a racing pulse, dry eyes, a dry mouth, and then i panic because i already deal with enough weird symptoms without adding more. i was hoping for something that would let me eat dinner and sleep through the night. instead i just felt high, uncomfortable, and still in pain. disappointing doesn't even cover it.

thc is a no from me. every time i try a product with thc in it, even a tiny amount, my pain seems sharper instead of better and my anxiety goes through the roof. i have sjogren's and the cotton-mouth from thc is honestly miserable enough on its own, but the worst part is feeling spacey and unable to tell whether i'm having a real flare or just getting weird from the oil. i've tried to give it multiple chances and it keeps letting me down.

does anyone else get basically zero benefit from cbd? i keep seeing it recommended everywhere for inflammation and sleep so i gave it a real shot for a month—tincture, gummies, even a topical balm. nothing. if anything i just felt more annoyed because i was spending money on stuff that did not touch the stiffness in my spine or the burning in my feet. i know people swear by it, but for me cbd has been a complete bust. maybe it helps anxiety for some people, but as far as my ra pain goes it has been useless.

my rheum mentioned medical marijuana like it was some miracle backup option, so i tried it after another brutal week of flares and insomnia. honestly i’m kind of disappointed. it didn’t calm the pain, it just made me foggy, anxious, and weirdly more aware of every ache in my hips and hands. i also woke up feeling hungover without having slept any better. maybe i reacted badly, but medical marijuana has not been the answer for me at all. if anything it made a bad night worse.

i keep seeing people suggest thc for autoimmune pain, but every time i try it my body feels worse, not better. the last time i used a low dose edible i got shaky, my heart raced, and my joints felt like they were screaming louder than before. i was hoping it would help with sleeping through the night, yet i ended up staring at the ceiling and waiting for the buzz to pass. thc is just not my friend, and i’m done pretending it’s worth another attempt.

vent: weed and sjogren's do not mix for me. i tried smoking on a weekend when my dryness and jaw pain were awful, thinking it might distract me or help me unwind. instead my mouth got drier, my throat felt scratchy, and i spent the whole evening chugging water and regretting it. i also got paranoid for no reason, which is the last thing i need when i'm already exhausted from this disease. people talk about weed like it fixes everything, but in my case it just added another miserable symptom.

has anyone else had their joint pain flare after cannabis? i used a small amount of an oil product because a friend insisted it would be gentle, but the next morning i was stiff in places that had actually been doing okay. it felt like my body hated it. i kept waiting for some relaxing effect, and all i got was nausea and a weird heavy feeling in my limbs. i’m starting to think cannabis is one of those things that sounds promising for inflammatory disease but just doesn’t work for me at all.

quick question for the people who tolerate thc: does it ever stop making you feel gross? i was hoping it would help me sleep with my RA pain, but instead i get foggy, nauseous, and then paranoid that every little twinge means i'm having a major flare. the weird part is the pain still doesn't budge. i just end up high, uncomfortable, and annoyed that i wasted money on something that doesn't touch the inflammation. i'm probably done experimenting with thc at this point.

i keep seeing people on here say weed is the only thing that gets them through a flare, and i wish that were true for me. i have ra and gave it a fair shot because nsaids upset my stomach, but the weed made me feel gross, disconnected, and weirdly more aware of every ache in my body. i also got a headache that lasted the rest of the day, which was super helpful /s. i’m not anti-anything, i just hate that this seems to be the one thing everyone suggests and it does absolutely nothing good for me.

anyone else feel like cbd is basically just expensive flavored oil? i bought a tincture after my rheumatologist said to “try it before upping the meds” and honestly i’m annoyed i spent the money. i have ra and my hands are the worst at night, but the cbd barely touched the pain and seemed to make me groggy without actually helping me sleep. i tried it for almost two weeks, different doses, under the tongue, in tea, all of it. nothing. if anything i woke up more stiff because i slept so lightly. i know some people swear by it, but for me cbd has been a complete letdown. i’m back to ice packs and my prescription stuff, which at least does something. has anyone actually had cbd help joint pain or am i just unlucky?

i’m starting to think thc and my body are not friends anymore. i have lupus and every time i take a tiny edible for pain, my heart starts pounding and my anxiety goes through the roof. the pain doesn’t even improve enough to be worth it, it just makes me feel weird, shaky, and more aware of every little symptom. last night i took 2.5mg thinking that was basically nothing, and i still ended up sitting on the couch convinced i was going to pass out. not fun. i used to tolerate thc years ago, but now it feels like it just magnifies everything bad. does this happen to anyone else after diagnosis, or should i just give up on thc entirely?

i wish weed worked for me because everyone in my family acts like it’s some miracle cure. i have ankylosing spondylitis and the stiffness in my back is brutal, especially in the morning. i’ve tried smoking weed a few times and all it did was make me feel spacey and a little nauseous while the pain stayed right where it was. once it even made me paranoid enough that i spent half the night thinking i was having a flare from hell. that was the final straw for me. i don’t judge people who use it and i’m glad it helps some folks, but for me weed is basically just a bad experience with no payoff. if anything, i’d rather take a naproxen and a heating pad and call it a day.

has anyone else had a bad reaction to medical marijuana for inflammation pain? my primary suggested i try it because i’m trying to avoid increasing my nsaids too much, and i figured maybe it would take the edge off my psoriatic arthritis. instead i felt cloudy, got super dry mouth, and the joint pain in my wrists seemed louder somehow. i don’t know how else to explain it, but i felt more aware of being uncomfortable rather than less uncomfortable. i also didn’t like how unsteady it made me feel walking around my apartment. maybe it helps some people, but medical marijuana has been a miss for me so far. i’m honestly frustrated because i wanted another option, not another thing to cross off the list.

i’m posting because i’m confused and a little annoyed. before i was diagnosed with sjogren’s, i used cannabis pretty casually and never had issues. after starting hydroxychloroquine and dealing with a flare, i tried cannabis again hoping it would help me relax and maybe sleep through the dryness and aching. nope. my throat felt even drier, my eyes burned more, and the next day i felt sluggish with zero pain relief. i don’t know if it’s the meds, the disease, or just me now, but cannabis seems to make the whole sicca thing worse instead of helping. i’m done pretending it’s some kind of magic fix.

i'm 34 and got diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis last year after months of thinking i was just being dramatic about the pain. the worst part for me has been mornings — my fingers feel like they're full of gravel until i move around for an hour. a friend keeps telling me to try cbd gummies because it 'takes the edge off,' but honestly cbd has done absolutely nothing for me except empty my wallet. i've tried two different brands now and i still wake up stiff, swollen, and exhausted. if anything i feel more annoyed because people keep acting like it's some miracle fix. has anyone else had zero luck with it? morning stiffness

anyone else get absolutely wrecked by thc? i have lupus and was hoping a little thc might help with sleep during flares, but it just makes me feel weird and panicky. my heart starts racing, i overthink every little body sensation, and then i end up even more aware of the pain. i gave it a few tries with different edibles and tinctures, same result every time. i know some people swear by it, but for me thc is the opposite of helpful. at this point i'd rather deal with the aches than the anxiety spiral. sleep help? not from thc

my rheum nurse casually suggested marijuana when i mentioned my lower back pain and fatigue, which honestly caught me off guard. i know they were trying to be helpful, but marijuana is not a good option for me. i tried smoking years ago and it left me dizzy, nauseous, and feeling like my joints hurt more because i was so tense and paranoid. i already have enough going on with ankylosing spondylitis without adding that on top. it feels frustrating when people toss out marijuana like it's the same as actual treatment. has anyone else had doctors/family push that at them? unwanted suggestions

i'm in a weird place with all the cannabis advice people keep giving me. i have ra and ulcerative colitis, and every time i mention pain or poor appetite someone tells me to 'just try cannabis.' i've done it. multiple times. it does not agree with me at all — i get foggy, my anxiety spikes, and the joint pain is still there when the high wears off. it feels like everyone around me thinks cannabis is some magic wellness shortcut, but for me it just makes me feel out of control. i'm tired of being told i'm not open-minded enough. no thanks, cannabis is not my answer

has anyone here actually had a bad experience with medical marijuana? i was diagnosed with sjogren's a few months ago and my cousin keeps pushing me to get a card because it supposedly helps with pain, dry eyes, sleep, everything. i tried a vape once and spent the entire night nauseous and staring at the ceiling, convinced i was having palpitations. my mouth was dry enough already, so that did not exactly improve things. i know medical marijuana helps some people, but i'm starting to think it's one of those things everyone recommends because it sounds natural, not because it works for everyone. i'm just looking for something that won't make me feel worse

has anybody else gotten absolutely nothing from cbd? i kept hearing it was the "safe" option, so i tried gummies, tinctures, and a cream for my hands. all it did was make me feel weird and a little queasy, and the pain in my wrists was still there when i woke up. i have ra and i really wanted this to be the thing that helped me sleep, but honestly cbd just feels like expensive disappointment at this point.

i'm sure people mean well, but i'm getting tired of every relative and coworker suggesting medical marijuana like it's some miracle cure. i have sjogren's and inflammatory arthritis, and i'm already juggling meds, labs, and side effects. the last thing i need is another thing that makes my head foggier or upsets my stomach. has anyone else had zero luck with medical marijuana for joint pain and fatigue? because so far it has done less than nothing for me.

i tried a low dose thc edible last night because my back and hips were flaring up and i couldn't sleep. bad idea. my heart started racing, i felt panicky for no reason, and the pain was still there except now i was anxious on top of it. i have lupus and i was hoping thc might take the edge off, but it honestly made the whole night worse. never again, i think.

weed used to be something i associated with relaxing, but after my psoriatic arthritis diagnosis it just seems to make me feel gross. i tried smoking a few times for pain and all i got was a dry mouth, a weird headache, and more awareness of how stiff my fingers are. maybe it works for other people, but for me it didn't help the inflammation or the sleep at all. just felt like i was wasting money and making myself feel worse.

quick rant: cannabis is apparently the answer to everything if you listen to people who don't have chronic illness. i've got ankylosing spondylitis and i've experimented with it more than i wanted to, mostly because i was desperate. every time i tried it, i ended up more spaced out and less able to tell whether my pain was actually better or i just didn't care as much. the only thing it changed was my motivation to do anything productive. not worth it for me.

has anyone else had weird reactions to cbd? i keep seeing people recommend it for inflammation and sleep, so i picked up a tincture and tried a tiny dose before bed. instead of helping, it made me feel anxious and sort of jittery, and the next morning my joints felt even more achy. i have ra and i already deal with enough random flares without my nighttime routine making things worse. maybe it was the brand, maybe it was the dose, but honestly i'm done experimenting for now. i was hoping cbd would be a gentle option and it just wasn't for me at all.

i wish thc worked the way people describe it online, because for me it is basically a guaranteed bad time. i have psoriatic arthritis and tried a low-dose gummy on a rough night when my shoulders and hands were on fire. within an hour i was dizzy, nauseous, and weirdly more aware of every single pain signal in my body. i did not get relief, just panic and a pounding heart. if anything the thc made it harder to sleep because i kept focusing on whether my skin was flushing and whether i was breathing normally. no thanks.

weed and autoimmune fatigue is such a frustrating combo for me. i know some people swear it helps them relax, but every time i smoke or even use a vape, my mouth gets so dry that i wake up feeling worse, and my joints are still stiff the next morning. i have spondyloarthritis and was really hoping weed would take the edge off pain + insomnia. instead i feel groggy, dehydrated, and kind of out of it without any actual pain relief. i keep wanting to believe i just haven't found the right strain, but after several tries i'm starting to think it just isn't worth it for my body.

my rheumatologist did not actually recommend medical marijuana, but a friend with lupus kept telling me to try it for appetite and pain, so i did. honestly, i hated it. it made me feel detached and sort of trapped inside my own head, and the pain was still there, just harder to ignore because i was also battling the side effects. i already have enough brain fog from my disease and meds; adding more fuzziness is the opposite of helpful. maybe medical marijuana is great for other people, but for me it was expensive, irritating, and not even remotely useful.

i'm so tired of people acting like cannabis is the miracle answer for every rheumatic disease symptom. i tried it twice for sleep and pain during a flare and both times it made my heart race and my muscles feel even more tense. i have inflammatory arthritis and when i'm already exhausted, the last thing i need is to feel spaced out and paranoid on top of it. the weirdest part is that it didn't touch the actual pain at all. i would much rather stick with my regular meds and a heating pad than go through that again.

anyone else feel like cbd is basically a waste of money for inflammatory arthritis? i’ve tried gummies, tinctures, even a pricey topical my friend swore by, and all it’s done is make me sleepy while my wrist and knees stay angry. i’m on methotrexate for psa and i was hoping cbd might take the edge off on bad days, but honestly it hasn’t touched the pain once. starting to wonder if it’s just marketing hype dressed up as miracle medicine.

i used to think marijuana was helping me with sleep until my lupus started flaring harder and i realized it was making my head foggy, my heart race, and my fatigue worse the next morning. i stopped for two weeks and felt weirdly clearer, even though the pain was still there. not saying it’s like that for everyone, but for me marijuana seems to do more harm than good.

quick question for people with ra: does thc make your joints feel worse too? i tried a low-dose edible last night because i was desperate after a shoulder flare, and instead of relaxing i got shaky, paranoid, and somehow more aware of every ache in my body. the pain never really improved, just my anxiety got louder. pretty disappointed because i’d hoped thc would be a decent backup when nsaids aren’t enough.

i know weed helps some people, but it does not play nice with my sjogrens at all. every time i smoke, my mouth gets so dry it feels like i’ve swallowed cotton and my eyes burn for hours. on top of that, it leaves me groggy without touching the stiffness in my hands. at this point i’m honestly done pretending weed is worth it for symptom relief.

my rheum mentioned medical marijuana as an option while we wait to see if my biologic starts working, so i gave it a real shot for the last month. different ratios, different brands, oils and edibles, all of it. no meaningful pain relief, and some nights it actually made my muscles tense up more and my stomach worse. if anything, medical marijuana has just added another expensive thing to the list of treatments that didn’t help.

has anyone else had their rheum suggest cbd like it's some kind of cure-all? i tried a tincture for my hand and wrist pain this week and honestly it did nothing except make me tired and weirdly foggy. my joints still hurt, my sleep was worse, and i felt kind of off the next day. i know people swear by it, but cbd has been a letdown for me so far. i'm sticking with the meds my doctor actually prescribed because at least those have evidence behind them.

i keep seeing people in autoimmune groups talk about cannabis as if it's the answer to everything. i gave it a real try after a bad flare of my psoriatic arthritis, and it just made me anxious and more aware of every ache in my body. no pain relief, just a racing heart and a miserable night. maybe it helps some folks, but cannabis seems to do the opposite for me. pretty disappointed because i really wanted it to be useful.

my pain clinic basically pushed me toward medical marijuana because i can't take nsaids regularly and they said it might help with the nerve pain and stiffness. i was hopeful, but after a few tries it mostly left me groggy, dry-mouthed, and weirdly panicky. my shoulders and hips were still on fire, so i don't see the point. i'm not anti-anything, i just hate when medical marijuana is sold like a miracle and then it ends up being another expensive thing that doesn't touch the inflammation.

quick vent: thc and i do not get along at all. i took a tiny edible for a flare night thinking it might help me relax, and instead i spent three hours convinced my chest pain meant something catastrophic was happening. my hands were still swollen, my back still hurt, and the only new symptom was full-blown anxiety. never again. i know some people use thc for pain, but for me it's just a panic trigger with a side of dry mouth.

weed used to be something i thought i'd be able to use on the rough days, especially with this stupid autoimmune fatigue, but it has honestly been awful for me. it makes my head spin, my mouth feel like sandpaper, and i end up hyper-focusing on every little symptom until i feel 10x worse. no relief, no chill, just discomfort. if anything, weed seems to make my pain tolerance lower. i'm jealous of the people who say it helps them, because it has been a hard no from me.

hi all, 28f with suspected seronegative RA here. my chiropractor and a friend both kept pushing cbd so i gave it a real try: tincture at night, cream on my hands, even gummies. honestly it did basically nothing for my pain and just left me groggy and weirdly spaced out the next day. i was hoping cbd would take the edge off my morning stiffness, but nope. if anything, i felt more tired and less able to get moving. anyone else get zero benefit from cbd? or am i just one of those people it doesn't touch at all?

has anyone else had a bad reaction to thc after developing autoimmune stuff? i have sjogren's + fibromyalgia and tried a tiny thc edible last week because i was desperate for sleep. within an hour my heart was racing, my mouth felt even drier than usual, and i got this awful spiral of anxiety for no reason. i used to tolerate it fine before i got sick, but now thc just seems to make everything worse. definitely not the relaxing experience people always talk about.

i'm getting so frustrated with all the 'just try cannabis' advice. i have lupus and inflammatory arthritis, and i swear cannabis does not help me at all. every time i've tried it, my pain feels louder, my head gets foggy, and i end up more useless than before. i know people mean well, but i'm tired of being told it's some miracle fix when my body clearly hates it. does anyone else feel like cannabis just adds another problem instead of solving one?

weed used to be my go-to in college, but after my ra diagnosis it flipped on me completely. even a couple puffs now make my joints feel oddly heavy and my brain turns to mush, which is the opposite of what i need when i'm already fighting fatigue. i also get this weird jittery feeling and then i spend the whole evening convinced i'm flaring harder. not fun, not helpful, and honestly i'm done pretending weed is for everyone.

i finally tried medical marijuana because my rheumatologist's office had a brochure about pain control and i was curious. big mistake. it made my mouth feel like sandpaper, my eyes burned, and my anxiety shot up instead of calming down. with sjogren's, the dryness alone was enough to make me quit, but the brain fog was the final straw. i know it helps some people, just not me, and i'm a little annoyed i spent money on it to feel worse.

has anyone else had cbd do absolutely nothing except make them feel weirdly foggy? i’ve got seronegative ra and my hands are on fire most mornings, so i figured a tincture might take the edge off. instead i got a dry mouth, a headache, and zero change in the joint pain. i gave it a solid 3 weeks too, not just one try. kind of annoyed because everyone in my family keeps talking about cbd like it’s some miracle plant and i’m sitting here still gripping a heating pad and waiting for it to kick in. did it just not work for me or can cbd actually make some people feel worse? maybe i’m missing something, but right now it feels like a waste of money.

i tried legal marijuana for the first time since being diagnosed with lupus and honestly it was awful. i thought it might help with the fatigue and aching, but instead my heart was racing, i got super anxious, and my joints felt more noticeable, not less. the next day i was also insanely dry and had a pounding headache. maybe i reacted badly, but it definitely did not feel like pain relief. i keep seeing people say marijuana helps autoimmune pain, so i’m wondering if anyone else has had it backfire like this or if i should just stay away from it completely.

weed has been a complete miss for me with psa. i used to think it was the one thing that actually took the edge off, but lately every time i try it my hands throb more, i get paranoid, and my skin feels hotter and itchier. i’m not sure if it’s the strain, the dose, or just my body changing, but i’m tired of hearing how weed is supposed to be this amazing anti-inflammatory option when it seems to do the opposite for me. has anyone else had it stop working and start making inflammation feel worse? honestly considering giving it up for good.

my rheumatologist didn’t recommend medical marijuana, but i brought it up because i’m running out of ideas for controlling pain between flares. big mistake. i tried it anyway after asking around, and all it did was make me dizzy, dry, and more exhausted the whole next day. i have inflammatory arthritis and probably the worst part was that the pain was still there, just with a weird buzz on top of it. not exactly what i expected from something so many people swear by. has anyone had a bad reaction like this and found out it was the strain or method, or is medical marijuana just not worth trying if you already deal with fatigue and dryness?

i tried thc gummies twice this month thinking maybe they’d help me sleep through a bad lupus flare. nope. first time i got sweaty, my heart was racing, and i ended up staring at the ceiling feeling panicky for 3 hours. second time was even worse, with more joint pain the next day and a horrible dry mouth that made my sjogren’s symptoms feel 10x worse. i know a lot of people swear by thc but it seems like it just sets off every annoying symptom i already have.

has anyone else been disappointed by medical marijuana for autoimmune pain? i have ra and my rheumatologist was fine with me trying it, but the results were basically nothing except an irritated throat and a foggy head the next morning. the strain recommendations, the expensive card, the dispensary trip... all of it felt like a big waste of time. i’m honestly surprised people keep recommending it for chronic inflammation when it didn’t touch my swelling or fatigue at all.

i know this probably won’t be popular, but weed makes my connective tissue symptoms feel worse, not better. i have mixed connective tissue disease and tried smoking a little with friends because everyone said it would help me relax. instead i got lightheaded, my hands were shaking, and my pain felt way more noticeable once i noticed it. maybe it’s just me, but i’ve had way better luck with rest, heat, and actual meds than with weed.

i’m just venting because i’m tired of hearing how cannabis is supposed to be this miracle option for everything. i have ankylosing spondylitis and tried it for nausea and pain after a rough medication switch, and it was a mess. bad headache, weird anxiety, and no real relief from the back pain. i’m not anti-everything, but cannabis was a letdown and i wish people would stop acting like it works for everyone with an autoimmune disease.
